text: Encapsulation means bundling data with the methods that guard it, and controlling access from outside.
A single leading underscore is a convention — it signals this attribute is internal, please don't touch it directly.
Python won't stop you, but other developers know to leave underscore-balance alone.
[chuckle] A double underscore goes further — Python name-mangles it, making it genuinely hard to reach by accident.
The idea is to expose safe methods, like deposit, that validate changes before touching the data.
[sniff] deposit refuses negative amounts, so the balance can only change through controlled, checked paths.
You read the balance through a method too, keeping the actual attribute protected inside.
[sigh] Reaching the double-underscore pin from outside fails, because Python renamed it behind the scenes.
[groan] Encapsulation is about trust and safety — expose a clean interface, and hide the fragile internals.
